title: Work
text:
Alongside my studies, I also have 7+ years of work experience where I have consistently delivered high-quality service while understanding the importance of teamwork, collaboration, and reliability. Learning to successfully balance demanding work commitments alongside full-time academic study demonstrates my strong abilities of time management and dedication.

Utrecht University | Research Assistant | Utrecht - (May 2026 – Present)
As a Research Assistant, I support the Data Donation Initiative (D3I) by contributing to research on digital trace data and data donation methodologies. My work involves systematically testing mobile applications, documenting their functionality through detailed action inventories, retrieving and assessing personal data exports to evaluate their structure and accessibility, and developing clear documentation to help future participants successfully access and donate their digital data.

title: A Little Bit More About Me…
text:
Hi, I’m Megan, and I love all things statistics. My journey began in high school, where I took an introductory statistics class and was introduced to the famous p-value. Since then, I have moved countries twice to pursue my studies in statistics, and I continue to be haunted by p-values. My main interest is biostatistics, so I feel very lucky to be completing an internship at UMC Utrecht, where I am writing my thesis for my master’s in Methodology and Statistics at Utrecht University. I am passionate about using data, methodology, and statistics to drive change and support those working in the medical field.
Outside of my studies, I enjoy music, films, and baking. On weekends, you will often find me at a concert (or even working a festival) and at the cinema, making the most of my Cineville pass!

title: Projects
text:
Interval Censoring within TwiCs | Methodology and Statistics for Behavioural, Biomedical and Social Science | Present
I am currently completing an internship at the Data Science & Biostatistics Department at UMC Utrecht, where I am writing my master’s thesis with the clinical trials team. My research explores interval censored methods using a simulation that replicates Trials within Cohorts (TwiCs), with the potential to extend the analysis to real cancer patient data. I am excited to see what the results reveal and to keep growing my understanding of statistics within the medical field. The project is expected to be completed in May 2027. For readers unfamiliar with TwiCs, see Figure 1 for a visual of such a trial.







Figure 1: Trials within Cohorts (TwiCs) design






Final Year Bachlors Thesis | Glasgow University | 2025 | First-Class Grade
I analysed real-world SEPA wastewater data to investigate flow and ammonia measurements in the context of wastewater-based epidemiology, independently sourcing and integrating supplementary rainfall data to strengthen the statistical analysis. Using R and Excel, I identified trends and patterns in the data and produced a comprehensive final report and presentation. Through this project, I developed strong skills in statistical analysis, critical thinking, and scientific communication, along with applied insight into medical and environmental statistics.
